issues.description: Constructor parameter order for class Lecture is inconsistent between the problem statement (which instructs students to follow the UML) and the provided solution. The UML in problem_statement.md lists the attributes in this order: numberOfInscribedStudents, lectureName, numberOfLecturers, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfTutors (problem_statement.md lines 63-68) and the text instructs the constructor to follow the UML (problem_statement.md lines 16-21). The solution's Lecture constructor signature is: Lecture(String lectureName, int numberOfInscribedStudents, int numberOfGuestStudents, int numberOfLecturers, int numberOfTutors) (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java line 13), which follows the textual attribute order instead of the UML order. This contradiction can confuse students about the expected parameter order and may cause mismatches with automated checks or example code.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor parameter order consistent across all artifacts. Either: (A) Update the solution and template constructor to match the UML order and examples (e.g. change the signature to: Lecture(int numberOfInscribedStudents, String lectureName, int numberOfLecturers, int numberOfGuestStudents, int numberOfTutors) and assign fields accordingly), or (B) update the UML and any textual instructions to match the constructor order used in the solution (Lecture(String lectureName, int numberOfInscribedStudents, int numberOfGuestStudents, int numberOfLecturers, int numberOfTutors)). Ensure the problem statement, UML diagram, template, and solution all show the same parameter order so students and automated checks are unambiguous.
